description: Automated management of local administrator account passwords on Windows domain-joined endpoints, ensuring each machine has a unique, cryptographically random password that rotates on a defined schedule. Legacy LAPS (AdmPwd.E) stores passwords as a confidential attribute on the computer object in AD, protected by ACLs. Windows LAPS (built-in to Windows 10 21H2+ and Server 2019+) adds password encryption using the machine's AD certificate and supports Azure AD-joined devices. LAPS eliminates the most common Windows lateral movement vector: shared local admin passwords set during imaging and never rotated. Without LAPS, compromising one machine's local admin hash (via SAM dump, Mimikatz, or volume shadow copy) enables Pass-the-Hash to every endpoint sharing that password. With LAPS, each hash works on exactly one machine and expires on the rotation schedule. Does not protect domain credentials, service accounts, or application-level credentials — only the local administrator account managed by the LAPS policy.

cvss_vector_impacts.rationale: Without LAPS, compromising one machine's local admin hash (SAM dump, Mimikatz) yields credentials valid on every machine sharing that password — confidentiality impact spans the entire fleet. With LAPS, each machine has a unique random password, so a stolen hash provides admin access only to the single compromised endpoint. Impact is reduced from fleet-wide credential exposure to single-machine access

In environments with shared local admin passwords, any local admin compromise effectively changes scope to other machines via Pass-the-Hash — the vulnerability impacts resources beyond the vulnerable component. With LAPS, the compromised credential works only on the originating machine, containing the blast radius to the vulnerable component's security authority. Does not prevent lateral movement via domain credentials, shared service accounts, or non-credential scope changes (VM escape, container escape)

verification.method: Verify LAPS policy enforcement via registry (legacy or Windows LAPS) and confirm managed password exists in AD

commands.command: Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft Services\AdmPwd' -Name AdmPwdEnabled -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -ExpandProperty AdmPwdEnabled
Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft Services\AdmPwd' -Name PasswordComplexity -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -ExpandProperty PasswordComplexity

remediation.name: Windows LAPS policy configuration via registry

steps.description: Enable legacy LAPS (AdmPwd.E) via registry policy. For Windows LAPS (built-in to Server 2022+/Win 11 22H2+), the built-in client is already present and this step configures the policy backing store.
steps.command: New-Item -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft Services\AdmPwd' -Force | Out-Null; Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft Services\AdmPwd' -Name AdmPwdEnabled -Value 1 -Type DWord

steps.description: Set password complexity to large letters + small letters + numbers + specials (complexity 4), length 20 characters, and 30-day rotation
steps.command: Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft Services\AdmPwd' -Name PasswordComplexity -Value 4 -Type DWord; Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft Services\AdmPwd' -Name PasswordLength -Value 20 -Type DWord; Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft Services\AdmPwd' -Name PasswordAgeDays -Value 30 -Type DWord

steps.description: Trigger an immediate password rotation to apply the new policy to the local administrator account

remediation.verify: Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft Services\AdmPwd' -Name AdmPwdEnabled -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -ExpandProperty AdmPwdEnabled

references.source: Microsoft — Configure Windows LAPS policy settings

relationships.rationale: LAPS replaces default/shared local admin passwords with unique auto-generated passwords per endpoint, eliminating the default credential attack surface
Automated rotation ensures local admin passwords are not static or hardcoded in imaging templates; does not address hardcoded credentials in application code
LAPS generates cryptographically random passwords meeting configurable complexity requirements, removing human password selection from local admin accounts
